description: Golden evaluation dataset for the Smart Itinerary Planner & Booking Assistant (Phase 6, Task 6.1). Each scenario is a multi-stop travel request paired with the exact deterministic outputs of src/tools/* (weather, attractions, transit, booking are all hash-seeded / registry-driven with no network calls, so tool-level expectations below are exact and reproducible) plus the expected multi-agent routing, guardrail, and HITL behavior a compliant coordinator run should produce. evals/run_evals.py (Task 6.2) is expected to: (1) replay expected_tool_calls directly against src/tools/* and assert exact matches -- this measures 'tool success rate'; (2) assert the coordinator/specialist wiring in expected_routing matches src/agents/* factories -- this measures 'model routing accuracy'; (3) run guardrail assertions (src/guardrails/budget_guardrail.py, src/guardrails/hitl_manager.py) against expected_guardrails -- this measures 'budget adherence' and HITL compliance; (4) score end-to-end agent transcripts against success_criteria as a qualitative 'planning accuracy' rubric (LLM-as-judge or human review), since the coordinator's natural-language itinerary synthesis is not itself deterministic.

sentinel_values.<generated>: Field is produced at runtime (e.g. a uuid4-derived booking id or confirmation token) and cannot be pinned in a golden file. Validate shape via the paired '*_pattern' regex instead of exact equality.
sentinel_values.<any>: Field value is intentionally unconstrained for this assertion.

schema_notes.tool_call_shape: Each expected_tool_calls[].expected mirrors the exact JSON produced by ToolResultEnvelope.model_dump_json() / ToolErrorEnvelope.model_dump_json() in src/tools/base.py -- {status:'success', data:{...}} or {status:'error', error_code, message, recovery_instruction}.
schema_notes.location_registry_note: src/tools/weather_tool.py, attraction_tool.py, and transit_tool.py all key their local geocoding stand-in on the *exact lowercased free-text query string*, not on any parsed city/country pair. 'Paris', 'London', and 'Springfield' are the only three registry entries with more than one match and are therefore always LOCATION_AMBIGUOUS; every other registered city ('Tokyo', 'Rome', 'Barcelona', 'New York', 'San Francisco') always resolves cleanly.

scenarios.title: Barcelona -> Rome relaxed city-hopping trip, within budget
scenarios.user_prompt: Plan a relaxed 4-day trip: 2 nights in Barcelona then 2 nights in Rome, September 10-14, 2026. I like outdoor spots and history, budget-tier moderate, total budget $1800. Book a hotel in each city and figure out how I get from Barcelona to Rome.

expected_routing.rationale: Fast forecast lookups for both cities before finalizing outdoor plans.
Search each city's catalog filtered by category/budget_tier/duration.
Coordinator owns calculate_transit_route_estimate directly for cross-stop routing.
Stage hotel reservations and gate confirmation on explicit HITL authorization.
Final multi-stop synthesis and budget/grounding guardrail pass.

expected.message: Route from 'Barcelona, Spain' to 'Rome, Italy' spans ~9457 km, which exceeds the realistic maximum for travel_mode='driving' (800 km).
expected.recovery_instruction: Retry with travel_mode='flight' for long-distance routes.

expected_tool_calls.note: Deliberately naive first attempt -- the coordinator must recover by retrying with travel_mode='flight' per recovery_instruction, not give up or hallucinate a route.

expected.message_contains: has not been explicitly authorized by the traveler in this conversation
expected.source: before_confirm_booking_tool_callback in src/guardrails/hitl_manager.py, not the underlying booking_tool

expected_tool_calls.note: Confirmation attempted before the traveler said yes -- must be blocked by the HITL gate even though the token is correct.

success_criteria: Final itinerary lists Park Guell and Colosseum & Roman Forum with no invented attractions.
Transit leg is presented as a flight (not driving) after the ROUTE_NOT_SUPPORTED recovery.
Total estimated cost ($1694.84) is reported as within the $1800 budget.
Neither hotel is confirmed until the traveler explicitly authorizes it in conversation.

scenarios.title: Tokyo luxury nightlife weekend that blows the stated budget
scenarios.user_prompt: 3 days in Tokyo, October 1-3 2026. I want the luxury nightlife scene -- Golden Gai bar hopping, nice hotel. My total budget is only $400 though.

expected_routing.rationale: Find nightlife options at the requested luxury tier.
Stage the hotel and activity cost so the coordinator can run the budget guardrail before proposing any confirmation.
Run evaluate_budget, detect the ceiling is exceeded, and halt before requesting booking authorization.

hitl.reason: Non-negotiable budget rule in src/agents/constitution.py must halt the flow at the guardrail before the coordinator ever asks the traveler to authorize a confirmation.

success_criteria: Agent surfaces the $140.00 overage explicitly and by exact amount, not a vague 'this might be too expensive'.
Agent asks the traveler to either raise the budget ceiling or downgrade the hotel/activity, and does not proceed to request booking authorization.
confirm_reservation_booking is never invoked in this scenario.

scenarios.title: Paris -> Rome trip where 'Paris' is never disambiguated by the traveler
scenarios.user_prompt: I want to visit Paris then Rome next month, roughly 2 days each.

expected_routing.rationale: Attempt forecast lookup for the first stop.
Surface the LOCATION_AMBIGUOUS candidates to the traveler and pause planning for that stop rather than guessing.

expected.message: Multiple matches found for 'Paris': Paris, France, Paris, Texas, USA, Paris, Ontario, Canada.
expected.recovery_instruction: Ask the user to specify the country/state, or retry with 'City, Country' format, e.g. 'Paris, France'.

expected.message: Multiple matches found for 'Paris': Paris, France, Paris, Texas, USA, Paris, Ontario, Canada.
expected.recovery_instruction: Ask the user to specify the country/state, or retry with 'City, Country' format, e.g. 'Paris, France'.

expected.message: Multiple matches found for origin='Paris': Paris, France, Paris, Texas, USA, Paris, Ontario, Canada.
expected.recovery_instruction: Ask the user to specify the country/state for origin, or retry with 'City, Country' format, e.g. 'Paris, France'.
Ask the user for a more specific or differently spelled destination.

expected_tool_calls.note: Confirms the known_limitation below: the tool's own suggested retry format does not actually resolve against the current registry.

known_limitations: src/tools/weather_tool.py, attraction_tool.py, and transit_tool.py resolve locations by exact-matching the full lowercased query string against _LOCATION_REGISTRY / _CITY_REGISTRY, whose only multi-match keys ('paris', 'london', 'springfield') are single bare words. Their own LOCATION_AMBIGUOUS recovery_instruction suggests retrying in 'City, Country' format (e.g. 'Paris, France'), but that string is not a registry key and step 4 above shows it returns LOCATION_NOT_FOUND instead of resolving. A compliant agent's only correct move today is to ask the traveler to pick a *different, unambiguous* city name, or the traveler must independently know to avoid 'Paris'/'London'/'Springfield' entirely -- true disambiguation is not currently achievable through the tool contract. This should be tracked as a backlog fix (e.g. registry keys on normalized 'city, country' strings) and evals/run_evals.py should flag this scenario as a known-broken retry path rather than a coordinator defect.
success_criteria: Agent never guesses which 'Paris' the traveler means and never fabricates a resolved_location.
Agent relays all three candidate cities (France, Texas, Ontario) to the traveler verbatim.
Agent does not claim the ambiguity was resolved by retrying with 'City, Country' format, since that retry demonstrably fails against the current tool implementation.

scenarios.title: Springfield -> London -> New York family trip with several agent mis-steps to recover from
scenarios.user_prompt: Family trip: a couple days in Springfield, then London, then New York City. We like shopping and family-friendly stuff, budget tier moderate. Also give me New York weather for November 1-20.

expected_routing.rationale: Forecast lookups, including the intentionally-too-long New York window.
Search filters, including deliberately invalid ones the coordinator must correct before retrying.

expected.message: Multiple matches found for 'Springfield': Springfield, Illinois, USA, Springfield, Missouri, USA, Springfield, Massachusetts, USA.
expected.recovery_instruction: Ask the user to specify the country/state, or retry with 'City, Country' format, e.g. 'Paris, France'.

expected.message: Multiple matches found for 'London': London, United Kingdom, London, Ontario, Canada.
expected.recovery_instruction: Ask the user to specify the country/state, or retry with 'City, Country' format, e.g. 'Paris, France'.

expected.message: Requested range spans 20 days; forecasts are only available up to 14 days out.
expected.recovery_instruction: Narrow the date range to 14 days or fewer, or tell the user long-range forecasts aren't available.

expected_tool_calls.note: Coordinator must narrow the window, not silently drop the weather check for New York.

expected.message: No attractions found in New York City, USA matching category='family', budget_tier='free', duration_hours=0.5.
expected.recovery_instruction: Retry with a higher duration_hours, a higher budget_tier, or omit category to broaden the search.

expected_tool_calls.note: Deliberately narrow first attempt; coordinator should broaden budget_tier and/or duration_hours per the recovery_instruction.
'ultra' is a typo'd/hallucinated tier name -- exercises the VALIDATION_ERROR path so the coordinator must self-correct to a real tier, not ask the traveler to rephrase.

New York's catalog only has one 'shopping' entry and it is luxury-tier; the coordinator must broaden budget_tier to 'luxury' (and tell the traveler there's no cheaper shopping option in the catalog) rather than keep retrying 'moderate'.

known_limitations: Springfield and London ambiguity share the same unresolvable-retry limitation documented in the paris_ambiguous_multi_stop scenario; this scenario intentionally exercises it a second time against different registry entries for regression coverage.
success_criteria: Agent asks the traveler to pick a specific Springfield and London before proposing itinerary items for those stops.
Agent narrows the New York weather window to 14 days or fewer instead of failing silently or fabricating a forecast.
Agent self-corrects the invalid budget_tier without asking the traveler to resend the request.
Final New York shopping recommendation is Fifth Avenue Shopping with an explicit note that it's the only (luxury-tier) shopping option in the catalog, not an invented budget-friendly alternative.

scenarios.title: New York -> San Francisco trip testing mandatory weather checks for outdoor activities and a mismatched confirmation token
scenarios.user_prompt: 5 days: New York November 5-7, then San Francisco November 8-9, 2026. I want an outdoor walk in both cities plus one indoor backup, and book a hotel in each city. Total budget $2200.

expected_routing.rationale: Mandatory per constitution.py's non-negotiable rule: outdoor activities must be weather-checked before scheduling.
Find the outdoor activity plus an indoor fallback in each city.
Cross-reference forecasts against candidate dates and pick the lower-risk day for each outdoor activity.
Stage both hotels; gate confirmation on HITL.

expected_tool_calls.note: Indoor backup for the New York outdoor slot, in case the coordinator's preferred day still looks weather-risky.

expected.message: Route from 'New York City, USA' to 'San Francisco, USA' spans ~11644 km, which exceeds the realistic maximum for travel_mode='driving' (800 km).
expected.recovery_instruction: Retry with travel_mode='flight' for long-distance routes.

expected.source: confirm_reservation_booking in src/tools/booking_tool.py (past the HITL gate, which passed because the booking was authorized -- the token itself is simply wrong)

expected_tool_calls.note: Distinguishes the HITL-layer AUTHORIZATION_REQUIRED (missing traveler consent) from the tool-layer AUTHORIZATION_REQUIRED (consent given, but wrong token supplied -- e.g. a typo or stale value).

budget_check.note: The San Francisco hotel (SFO-HTL-06, $250.00) is staged and confirmed analogously to step 8-10; omitted above for brevity since it is not needed to exercise a new tool-error path.

weather_safety_rule.rule_source: src/agents/constitution.py NON_NEGOTIABLE_RULES, 'mandatory weather checks for outdoor activities'
weather_safety_rule.expected_behavior_if_scheduled_on_2026-1: Agent must flag the 'thunderstorms' condition and either move the walk to 2026-11-05 or swap in the Metropolitan Museum of Art indoor backup for that day.
2026-11-08 carries 87% precipitation probability (highest of the trip); agent must not schedule the only outdoor activity on this day without an explicit weather caveat to the traveler.

success_criteria: Central Park Stroll is scheduled on 2026-11-05, not 2026-11-06 (thunderstorms) -- or, if scheduled on 11-06, is paired with an explicit weather warning and the Met Museum offered as an alternative.
Golden Gate Bridge Walk is scheduled on 2026-11-09 (sunny) rather than 2026-11-08 (87% precipitation), or carries an explicit rain caveat if not.
Transit is presented as a flight after the driving attempt fails.
A wrong confirmation token is reported back to the traveler with a clear ask to re-share the correct code, not silently retried or treated as success.

scenarios.title: Tokyo -> Rome business trip stress-testing the HITL gate end to end
scenarios.user_prompt: Business trip: Tokyo December 1-2, then Rome December 3-4, 2026. Book me a flight from Tokyo to Rome, $650 max for the flight.

expected_routing.rationale: Stage the flight and enforce the HITL gate around confirm_reservation_booking via before_confirm_booking_tool_callback.

expected_tool_calls.note: Never let a correct token alone finalize a booking -- BookingAgent must not call this before the traveler has said yes, and the callback must block it if it tries anyway.

expected.recovery_instruction: No action needed; this booking was already finalized. Do not retry the confirmation.

expected_tool_calls.note: Idempotency/re-confirmation guard: repeating an already-confirmed booking must not double-charge or error opaquely.

expected.message: No staged booking found for provisional_booking_id 'book_doesnotexist'.
expected.recovery_instruction: Call stage_provisional_booking first, or double-check the provisional_booking_id for typos.

expected_tool_calls.note: Guards against confirming a hallucinated or stale booking id.

success_criteria: The flight is only confirmed after an explicit, in-conversation traveler authorization is recorded via authorize_booking.
A second confirmation attempt on the same booking is rejected with a clear 'already confirmed' message, not treated as a fresh success.
An attempt to confirm a booking id that was never staged is rejected with RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND, not a crash or a fabricated confirmation.
